notes: Fix: the motor terminal ports on the controller board are now kind 'lead' instead of 'lug'. The motors' own ports are leads, and lead-to-lead is a compatible join. The parts are the same as before.
The motor controller board was not found by lookup_part, so it stays a new part type. Its header ports GPIO7, GPIO8, GPIO9 and GPIO10 are the pins the tutorial names.
Battery red wire goes to VIN and black wire to GND, as the manual requires.
Motors can go either way round on their terminal blocks. Motor 1 goes to Motor B and motor 2 to Motor A, with motor pin 1/2 chosen arbitrarily.
The board sits on the whole 40-pin header. Only the GPIO pins the tutorial names (7, 8, 9, 10) are modelled. The board's other header pins, including ground, are not modelled.
The battery pack, motors and Pi have attached wires, so no separate jumper wires are listed. No breadboard is used.
